specAmbiguitiesResolved: fault_window_id is the rule's fault_window_key; rules sharing a key on an asset (and manual reports naming such a rule) converge on one incident. Fault family is triage data on the incident, not a dedupe dimension.
Opening runs DETECTED -> TRIAGING in the same transaction (guard: incident and source evidence persisted); acknowledgement is a separate versioned record, not a transition, and resets on reopen.

Deadline basis TRIGGER_EVENT_AT = breach onset (first reading of the qualifying run) in source event time, or the report's observed time (<= 5 s ahead, <= 24 h old); OPENED_AT = database opening time. Reopen keeps the original deadline ledger (no second SET) and expires it if it already passed.

Bounded lateness: the newest LIVE reading must be at most maxEvaluationLagMs old at the evaluation instant; the instant is never behind the database clock and at most 1 h ahead (consumers use the batch receipt time). Samples beyond the instant are ignored.
Watch window: the RECOVERED incident's pinned rule watch_window_ms, with the trigger's newest event after recovered_at and the evaluation instant within recovered_at + window.
Policy revision pinned = the AUTHORITY policy revision in force at opening (nullable when a tenant has none); rule and procedure revisions are pinned separately.

Deadline authority: SHORTEN and RESUME need incident.manage; PAUSE and EXTEND additionally need the pinned procedure's adjust_role at the site, its pause allowance and its total extension bound. Incident pause does not pause the deadline.

Ownership: assignees are ACTIVE members with operator/maintenance_approver/engineer/admin at the site; escalation re-entry, pause, resume and handoff need the accepted current owner; handoff targets someone else and needs a future due time.

Resume revalidation (M04 part): asset ACTIVE and, when the prior state is AWAITING_APPROVAL/EXECUTING/VERIFYING, the pinned asset revision still current; later modules add checks via ResumeRevalidator. M01 has no PAUSED -> ESCALATED edge, so a failed revalidation leaves the incident PAUSED (POLICY_HOLD).

Stale-data behaviour ESCALATE_ACTIVE: telemetry.stale.v1 for a device escalates active incidents on its currently assigned assets with a STALE_SIGNAL and signal_state UNCERTAIN (sticky until accepted-owner re-entry); HOLD does nothing. Stale data never recovers or de-escalates.

Idempotency-Key receipts are unique per tenant and key across all incident commands; the request digest covers command type, principal and body. Engine triggers are deduplicated by signal digest instead.
Device corroboration on an open incident is incremental: only samples not yet linked are linked (each signal <= 500, total kept).

Main-path edges are requested by owning modules through advanceIncident with a guard reference; M04 enforces legality and CAS. RECOVERED is never reachable through advanceIncident; only the internal recovery hook with a PASSED evaluation from a RecoveryEvaluator can set it.

Reopen after the pinned deadline: the deadline is not recomputed (the ledger has one SET and the original is immutable); if the RUNNING deadline already passed, reopen appends EXPIRE under the pinned procedure so the incident shows EXPIRED/overdue (and the deadline sweep's escalation applies to later expiries). A new response deadline for a reopened incident needs a spec decision.
unresolvedRisks: signal_state UNCERTAIN is cleared only by accepted-owner re-entry, not automatically by fresh data.
Samples from a later-revoked device still count inside the window (revocation is not re-checked at evaluation).
The deadline sweep and the telemetry consumer must be scheduled by the deployed process (M14); nothing runs them on a timer here.
Engine paths (incident.engine) are open to every worker-role service identity and every outbox/job worker context of the tenant.
listIncidents/getIncidentTimeline are bounded (500 / 1000 rows per list, 20 000 linked samples) but not cursor-paginated for timelines; NFR-08 open-latency targets are recorded, not measured.
evidence_revisions has no asset column, so an evidence revision for an incident can still name another asset's revision (M05 should bind it).
No production RecoveryEvaluator exists: incidents cannot reach RECOVERED outside tests until M11 implements it (tests use an explicitly test-only fake evaluator).
A reopened incident whose deadline already passed is EXPIRED/overdue but not given a new deadline; the reopen does not itself escalate.
nextModuleInputs: Read APIs (incident.read at the incident's site, or engine workers): getIncident(pool, ctx, incidentId) -> IncidentView {state, version, pausedFromState, siteId, assetId, assetRevisionId, ruleRevisionId, procedureRevisionId, policyRevisionId, triggerKind/InputOrigin, urgency, faultFamily, faultWindowKey, dedupeKey, signalState, deadline{Kind,Basis,BasisAt,BasisDigest,TimezoneBasis}, originalResponseDeadlineAt, currentResponseDeadlineAt, deadlineStatus, currentAssignment, reopenCount, correlationId, openLatencyMs}; listIncidents(pool, ctx, {siteId?, assetId?, states?, activeOnly?, limit<=500, after?}); getIncidentTimeline -> transitions, signals (+ exact samples), assignments, deadlineEvents, manualReports (+ attachments), acknowledgements, riskEstimates (NON_AUTHORITATIVE).

Commands (all take expectedVersion + idempotencyKey; stale version -> VERSION_CONFLICT): acknowledgeIncident, assignIncident, acceptAssignment, handoffIncident, escalateIncident, returnFromEscalation, pauseIncident, resumeIncident(..., {revalidate}), reopenIncident, adjustIncidentDeadline (PAUSE/RESUME/SHORTEN/EXTEND), recordRiskEstimate; engine: evaluateIncidentRules, applyTelemetryStale, handleTelemetryEvent, expireIncidentDeadlines, advanceIncident({to: AWAITING_EVIDENCE|PLANNING|AWAITING_APPROVAL|EXECUTING|VERIFYING|RECOVERED|ESCALATED, guardRef, reasonCode}).

M05 (evidence/reasoning): bind evidence revisions to real incident ids (FK now enforced); move TRIAGING/REOPENED work forward with advanceIncident(to AWAITING_EVIDENCE|PLANNING, guardRef = evr_ id); fault_family/urgency on the incident are triage hypotheses, not authority; manual reports and signals are inputs with explicit trust labels.

M07 (notifications): consume incident.opened.v1 (payload.notification.required for CRITICAL), incident.reopened.v1, incident.state_changed.v1 (to ESCALATED), incident.assignment_changed.v1 and incident.deadline_changed.v1 with consumeOnce; delivery is never acknowledgement (acknowledgeIncident is a separate operator command).

M08 (planning) / M09-M10: read the pinned procedureRevisionId, currentResponseDeadlineAt and deadlineStatus as the containment deadline input (FR-09); never derive deadlines from risk estimates; request PLANNING -> AWAITING_APPROVAL -> EXECUTING -> VERIFYING through advanceIncident with plan/approval/intent references; AWAITING_APPROVAL -> PLANNING only before possible egress; supply ResumeRevalidator checks for plan/approval/in-flight effects.

M11 (recovery): implement RecoveryEvaluator in packages/incidents/src/recovery.ts terms (load the named rev_ evaluation in the caller's transaction; return it only when it is PASSED for this incident, its current action digest and pinned asset revision, with the stable LIVE post-boundary window and required signoffs) and expose a recovery command that calls the internal recoverIncidentWithEvaluation(pool, workerCtx, incidentId, {recoveryEvaluationId, reasonCode, expectedVersion, idempotencyKey}, evaluator); do not export the hook itself. Use the pinned rule recoveryWindowMs and asset revision; a recurrence inside the rule's watch window reopens the same incident automatically; stale/late/backfill samples are already excluded from incident evidence (UB043).
truthStatement: M04 completed and locally verified the incident engine (rule evaluation, database-enforced single active incident, lifecycle, ownership and deadline ledger, manual reports, notification triggers) against a local PostgreSQL 17 container with synthetic devices; no physical sensor, notification delivery, deployment, provider, Kite payment or recovery evidence exists, and all of it remains NOT_RUN.
